source_documents.title: Excited‐State Proton Transfer in Push‐Pull N‐Methyl Pyridium Reversible Super‐Photoacids Ruled by Intramolecular Hydrogen‐Bond‐Like Interactions

conditions_studied: buffered water, pH 4 to 11 and H0 -3

reference_evidence_units.quote: Fluorimetric titrations revealed a clear excited-state proton transfer (ESPT) with negative pKa* values for the two molecules with the phenol attached in ortho relative to the double bond, so as to be regarded as super-photoacids.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 2, 3

reference_evidence_units.quote: Conversely, no proton transfer was observed when the hydroxyl group was in the para position.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1
reference_evidence_units.statement: The para isomer shows no ESPT; its fluorimetric pKa equals the ground-state pKa (8.2 vs 8.5).

reference_evidence_units.quote: Quantum-mechanical calculations confirmed that intramolecular hydrogen-bond-like interactions, only attainable in the ortho isomers, are strengthened by the charge transfer process occurring upon excitation, resulting in enhanced acidity.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 1-3
reference_evidence_units.statement: In the ortho isomers an OH...H-C(vinyl) interaction strengthens on excitation and raises the acidity.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Ultrafast transient absorption and fluorescence up-conversion (UC) spectroscopies allowed direct observation of the ESPT process on the picosecond time scale, in agreement with the negative pKa*.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 2, 3
reference_evidence_units.statement: ESPT takes about 3 ps; the excited base emits near 650 nm.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The negative pKa* values obtained by the Förster cycle are in perfect agreement with the experimental ones for compounds 2 and 3, while a value of 2.0 was predicted for compound 1.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 1-3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Förster-cycle pKa*: negative for 2 and 3, 2.0 for 1.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The changes in electron densities revealed that a certain charge transfer from the phenolic ring to the methyl-pyridinium occurs upon excitation and becomes particularly important in the deprotonated molecules, where the phenolate is a better electron donor relative to the phenol
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 1-3
reference_evidence_units.statement: Excitation moves charge from the phenol (or phenolate) to the methylpyridinium.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The conjugated excited base returns to its ground state with a time constant of about 10 ps, because its pronounced push-pull character, by virtue of the enhanced electron acceptor strength of the deprotonated phenol, strongly favors internal conversion over fluorescence.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 2
reference_evidence_units.statement: The push-pull excited base decays in about 10 ps, mostly by internal conversion.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: Excitation-induced phenol-to-pyridinium charge transfer (TD-DFT); the paper does not use it to explain emission changes of 1.
